1. **P1 — Section 1, permission-mode detection.** The proposed scan order is not Claude Code’s settings precedence. Scalars resolve managed → CLI → local → project → user, so a project/local `defaultMode: default` legitimately overrides user-level `bypassPermissions`; the proposed managed → user scan would incorrectly short-circuit. It also calls file-based managed settings “effective” even though server/MDM policy may supersede those files. Current `/wrap` has only the simplistic project-file check at [wrap/SKILL.md:455](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/wrap/SKILL.md:455). [Claude’s settings precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence) also specifies base `managed-settings.json` followed by alphabetically merged drop-ins. Fix: resolve eligible values in the real order, merge managed files exactly, label the result approximate when CLI or non-file managed policy is unknowable, and preferably capture `permission_mode` through a hook event whose schema explicitly carries it, such as `UserPromptSubmit`.

2. **P1 — Section 1, `auto` semantics.** The plan explicitly says effective `auto` “never short-circuits,” contradicting the feature request and recreating the same permission-promotion hazard for auto-approved activity. It also handles `disableBypassPermissionsMode` but omits `disableAutoMode`; Claude documents both restrictions and says project/local `auto` and `bypassPermissions` values are inert on current versions. Fix: have the helper emit `EFFECTIVE_MODE`, short-circuit Step 4 for both effective `auto` and `bypassPermissions`, honor both disable keys, and add fixtures for higher-precedence non-auto overrides and disabled auto—not merely the four proposed fixtures. [Claude permission configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) defines those modes and disable keys.

3. **P1 — Section 9, bypass migration.** The migration can offer “enable bypass user-wide” when `BYPASS_SOURCE=disabled`, even though that write cannot take effect; it also exposes only one `INERT_PROJECT_MODE`, so two stale keys can leave one behind and prompt forever. No atomic removal/write mechanism is specified, encouraging the agent to hand-roll edits to user settings—the exact class of ambiguity this repo avoids with mutation helpers. Current init writes the stale key mechanically at [koji-init/SKILL.md:111](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/koji-init/SKILL.md:111), and `0g` is already occupied at [kick-off/SKILL.md:215](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/kick-off/SKILL.md:215). Fix: add a dedicated atomic migration helper that reports and removes all inert occurrences, suppress the user-wide option when disabled, call the new migration `0h`, and safely quote any sourceable path output.

4. **P1 — Sections 0 and 5, prompt-toggle validation.** Work item 0 says to emit wrap settings through `_resolve`, which accepts arbitrary strings; therefore `wrap.prompts: typo` is treated as “not on” and silently disables safety prompts. `_resolve` also consults global config after project config at [bin/koji-detect:64](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-detect:64), contradicting the decision that `wrap.*` is project-only. Fix: validate `WRAP_PROMPTS` and `WRAP_COMMIT_PROMPT` with an enum resolver that warns and fails safe to `on`, add a project-only resolver for the promised scope, and define whether explicit `commit_prompt: on` overrides `prompts: off` for commit-gate failures.

5. **P1 — Section 2b, duet-plan quota classification.** `koji-codex-classify` cannot safely classify prose critiques. It first looks for a JSON array and, when none exists, scans arbitrary stdout for words including `quota`, `429`, and `rate limit` at [bin/koji-codex-classify:34](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-codex-classify:34). A healthy plan review of this feature can therefore be misclassified as `QUOTA` simply because its critique discusses quota handling. Fix: add a prose/verdict mode that treats exit-zero output with a valid terminal `VERDICT:` as healthy before quota scanning, or create a separate duet-plan classifier; do not pin the unsafe phrase “only branches on QUOTA.”

6. **P1 — Section 2b, malformed Claude results fail open.** Writing `[]` for an unparseable Claude gate response makes the sole reviewer’s failure a PASS: `/duet-impl` computes zero HIGH findings and continues at [duet-impl/SKILL.md:205](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/duet-impl/SKILL.md:205). Likewise, the synthesizer deliberately maps missing/malformed inputs to empty findings at [bin/koji-duet-synthesize:49](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-duet-synthesize:49), potentially yielding PASS. Fix: retry malformed Claude output once; after that, record reviewer-unavailable and defer/fail closed for an impl gate, and explicitly mark a duet review degraded rather than pretending an empty reviewer completed successfully.

7. **P1 — Section 2b, backend-neutral contracts are incomplete.** The plan says only the reviewer-template heading/opening need neutralization, but later-round author prompts repeatedly say “codex” at [duet-plan/references/prompt-templates.md:93](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/duet-plan/references/prompt-templates.md:93), and the cross-review prompt begins “You are codex” at [duet-review/SKILL.md:356](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/duet-review/SKILL.md:356). More seriously, the synthesizer hard-codes `agreed_by`, severity fields, cross-review provenance, and `reviewers: ["claude","codex"]` at [bin/koji-duet-synthesize:84](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-duet-synthesize:84) and [bin/koji-duet-synthesize:345](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-duet-synthesize:345); display-only correction leaves `verdict.json` false. Fix: parameterize reviewer names throughout prompts and add actual backend metadata to the synthesizer/verdict schema while retaining stable A/B slot identifiers for compatibility.

8. **P1 — Section 2b, hybrid escalation state machine.** `koji-duet-backend plan-round` is specified as always returning Claude for `claude-rounds+codex-final`, yet after a rejected final gate the plan says all remaining rounds use codex. A stateless mapping cannot produce that transition, and “set done” is not durable across the fresh Bash blocks the plan itself calls out. At the round limit, a codex rejection also increments past the cap immediately, leaving no revision round despite claiming “remaining rounds”; current deadlock behavior begins at [duet-plan/SKILL.md:193](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/duet-plan/SKILL.md:193). Fix: persist an explicit phase marker, update the round-backend file before dispatch, define crash recovery from existing raw/exit files, and specify whether final-gate rejection deadlocks or grants a revision. Qualify “exactly one codex call” as the clean-consensus case.

9. **P1 — Section 2b, read-only mutation guard.** Hashing `git status --porcelain` detects path/status changes, not content changes inside an already-modified tracked file, so a reviewer can alter the diff without changing the hash. `md5` is also absent on many Linux systems, despite the repo already carrying a portable hash cascade at [bin/koji-detect:121](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-detect:121). Finally, `/duet-review` explicitly lets the user continue working while reviewers run at [duet-review/SKILL.md:112](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/duet-review/SKILL.md:112), so any detected movement is not attributable to the reviewer. Fix: hash binary staged/unstaged diffs plus untracked contents using a shared portable helper, word the result as unattributed concurrent movement, and invalidate/rebuild the review snapshot rather than merely adding a report note.

10. **P1 — Section 6, `--set-next-step` quoting.** Mirroring the current awk reader cannot meet the stated round-trip acceptance. `_fm_get` removes `#...` before considering quotes and strips outer quotes without unescaping `\"` at [bin/koji-plans-research:23](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-plans-research:23); thus `"confirm issue #123"` reads back truncated, while embedded quotes read back with backslashes. Passing arbitrary text through `awk -v` also interprets escapes, and newlines can inject frontmatter. Fix: enforce a one-line scalar, serialize with a real YAML-compatible quoted-scalar encoder (JSON string syntax is sufficient), decode it symmetrically in `_fm_get`, and test `#`, `:`, quotes, backslashes, CRLF, and rejected newline/tab input.

11. **P2 — Section 6, stale-next-step selection.** “Slug or next-step subject appears” never defines “subject,” tokenization, case handling, or the threshold for a match. It also cites current-session achievements/notes before Step 3 has written them: Step 2b starts at [wrap/SKILL.md:93](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/wrap/SKILL.md:93), while the session entry is created at [wrap/SKILL.md:421](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/wrap/SKILL.md:421). This invites another bespoke grep/awk implementation despite the repo’s explicit helper-first warning at [bin/koji-plans-research:322](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-plans-research:322). Fix: move the check after the session entry is finalized or persist the proposed entry text, and define a helper-backed candidate algorithm with exact inputs and output instead of “subject appears.”

12. **P1 — Section 4, amend eligibility.** The proposed predicate does not check the commit timestamp against the session-start sentinel, so “same-session” reduces to “some descendant commit by the configured author.” The sentinel is first-write-wins at [kick-off/SKILL.md:134](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/kick-off/SKILL.md:134), making this especially unsafe after an abandoned wrap. It also permits automatic amendment of a mixed worktree, which can fold unrelated new code into the previous commit, and “no remote-tracking ref contains HEAD” cannot guarantee never-pushed when refs are stale. Fix: require a normal attached single-parent HEAD, matching committer identity, commit time after the sentinel file’s creation time, and docs-only changes for automatic amend; make mixed amendment an explicit one-time choice and describe remote detection as “not known pushed” unless the remote is queried.

13. **P1 — Section 3, commit-gate mechanics.** “Run verbatim” does not say how a configured command containing arguments, pipes, environment assignments, or `&&` is executed; invoking the variable as one quoted executable will fail. “After staging” is also underspecified for split commits, and a gate that formats or generates files can pass while the staged snapshot remains stale. Current staging happens separately per strategy at [wrap/SKILL.md:509](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/wrap/SKILL.md:509). Fix: execute custom commands through a clearly documented shell, capture output/exit in a tempfile, run against each exact staged commit where relevant, detect gate-induced tree changes, restage and rerun, and make “fix-then-commit” loop through the gate again before committing.

14. **P1 — Section 7, placeholder gate.** The proposed matcher catches two named placeholders and `**Field**: [...]`, but the shipped templates contain many other forms: `[Category 1]`, `[Achievement 1]`, test checkboxes, and Notes placeholders in [templates/default/SESSION_TEMPLATE.md:1](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/templates/default/SESSION_TEMPLATE.md:1), plus different placeholders throughout [templates/simple/SESSION_TEMPLATE.md:1](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/templates/simple/SESSION_TEMPLATE.md:1). A generic bracket scan would falsely reject `[Claude]` and `[ ]`; the narrow scan misses required fields. The plan also deliberately omits the requested default AI-lens field, so the feature’s structural acceptance is not delivered. Fix: introduce an unambiguous required-value sentinel or explicit required-field metadata, gate only those markers, and either ship AI-lens with the opt-out requested or record that requirement as rejected rather than claiming it is implemented generically.

15. **P1 — Section 8, LOKO mode contract.** Appending a seventh field is not automatically backward-compatible: a six-variable Bash `read` folds the new tab and `mode` into the sixth variable. The current helper emits exactly six fields at [bin/koji-doc-status:156](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-doc-status:156), while `/wrap`, `/kick-off`, and `/inspect-doc-drift` document six-field records at [wrap/SKILL.md:172](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/wrap/SKILL.md:172), [kick-off/SKILL.md:514](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/kick-off/SKILL.md:514), and [inspect-doc-drift/SKILL.md:51](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/inspect-doc-drift/SKILL.md:51). The Pass C state machine also never says what happens when an already-on-demand entry is selected for demotion, permitting repeated suffixes. Fix: update every consumer/parser to seven variables, document the schema break, test `cut -f1-6` compatibility, and define transitions explicitly—e.g. `always → on-demand`, while already-on-demand entries are kept or separately proposed for removal.

16. **P1 — Verification and selfcheck.** The plan promises acceptance fixtures but lists only scratchpad/manual checks. `koji-selfcheck` explicitly says it is static marker lint, not a behavioral test, at [bin/koji-selfcheck:6](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/bin/koji-selfcheck:6); one occurrence of “fresh Agent context, never a fork” cannot protect every dispatch site. Also, `bash -n bin/*` checks only the first positional script, not every file, so the proposed syntax verification gives false coverage. Fix: check in executable regression fixtures for precedence, migration, frontmatter, backend mapping, escalation/resume, and LOKO parsing; loop over each Bash-shebang file for `bash -n`; compile-check the Python helper separately; and pin/count distinct operational markers for first-pass, gate, and cross-review dispatches.

17. **P2 — Section 2a, duet-plan heredoc fix.** The claimed command-substitution bug is not present: shell expansion is not recursively re-evaluated, so `$(...)` or backticks introduced by expanding `$PLAN_BODY` in the heredoc at [duet-plan/SKILL.md:228](/Users/h.b./.claude/skills/koji/duet-plan/SKILL.md:228) remain literal. Appending with `printf` is harmless, but the proposed test passes before the change and does not justify an independent “bug fix” commit. Fix: remove this item or reframe it solely as simpler output construction, with a test that demonstrates an actual behavioral difference.

What I would cut: defer the on-demand LOKO tier and the kick-off “may be stale” heuristic; both add new parsing/state transitions without addressing the three highest-risk fixes. Drop the nonexistent PLAN_BODY expansion bug entirely. Ship permission-mode correctness, stdin-based Codex invocation, commit gating, conservative amend, and a smaller reviewer-backend implementation with truthful provenance and persistent tests first.

Review-method note: I applied the `engineer` skill’s surgical, scope-first discipline and made no repository changes.

VERDICT: DISAGREE
